chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu al-Hasan al-Mazi (peace be upon him), who said:
He is not from us, the one who does not account for himself every day. So if he does good, he asks Allah for increase, and if he does evil, he seeks forgiveness from Allah for it and repents to Him.
ai.seo_question: What is the daily practice that distinguishes a true follower of the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of *muhasabah* (self-accounting) as a daily spiritual discipline, distinguishing the true adherent through proactive gratitude for good deeds and immediate repentance for sins. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on continuous self-reflection as a means to maintain spiritual equilibrium and closeness to God, rooted in the teachings of the Imams.
